skill.name: api-documenter
skill.description: Create and improve API specifications, reference content, developer portals, SDK guidance, examples, validation plans, and migration documentation.
skill.summary: Build accurate, maintainable API documentation for modern developer workflows.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: All three static findings are false positives caused by ordinary documentation language. The skill contains guidance only, with no network reconnaissance instructions, executable code, or prompt injection.

- Balances comprehensiveness with clarity and conciseness

finding_verdicts.reason: The cited text discusses documentation analytics and usage tracking. It does not instruct network scanning, host discovery, or collection of network infrastructure data.
The cited text describes prioritizing developer experience and time to first success. It contains no reconnaissance behavior, command, or network target.
The cited text is a writing principle about balancing completeness and clarity. It has no relationship to network discovery or probing.

content.value_statement: Incomplete API documentation slows integrations and increases support demand. This skill structures specifications, examples, portals, SDK guidance, validation, and migration content for developer audiences.
actual_capabilities: Authors and reviews OpenAPI 3.1 and AsyncAPI specifications.
Plans developer portals, navigation, onboarding, search, and interactive API exploration.
Creates authentication, webhook, error, migration, and deprecation documentation.
Designs SDK and code example generation workflows across multiple languages.
Proposes validation, contract testing, documentation deployment, analytics, and maintenance processes.
limitations: It does not execute specifications, generated SDKs, examples, or deployment workflows.
It requires source details to document endpoints, schemas, authentication, errors, and behavior accurately.
Generated content still needs validation against the deployed API and organizational security requirements.
Platform-specific implementation details may require documentation tool or infrastructure expertise.

use_cases.title: Publish a REST API Reference
use_cases.description: Turn endpoint requirements into a structured OpenAPI specification with authentication, request, response, and error guidance.

use_cases.title: Design a Developer Portal
use_cases.description: Plan navigation, onboarding, search, tutorials, interactive exploration, analytics, and support paths across multiple APIs.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Version Migration
use_cases.description: Explain breaking changes, compatibility concerns, upgrade steps, deprecation dates, and validation checks for existing integrations.

prompt_templates.title: Document One Endpoint
prompt_templates.prompt: Document this endpoint for new integrators: [endpoint details]. Include its purpose, authentication, parameters, responses, errors, and one realistic example.
prompt_templates.scenario: Create a focused reference entry from complete endpoint details.

prompt_templates.title: Review an API Specification
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this OpenAPI specification: [specification]. Identify missing schemas, unclear descriptions, incomplete examples, authentication gaps, and inconsistent error responses.
prompt_templates.scenario: Improve the quality and completeness of an existing specification.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Developer Portal
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a developer portal for [APIs] and [audiences]. Provide information architecture, onboarding journeys, search needs, interactive tools, governance, and success measures.
prompt_templates.scenario: Coordinate documentation across products and developer personas.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Documentation Delivery Strategy
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a documentation delivery strategy for [API program]. Cover contracts, SDK generation, example tests, deployment gates, versioning, migrations, analytics, ownership, and review cadence.
prompt_templates.scenario: Establish an advanced documentation workflow across teams.

output_examples.input: Document the customer lookup endpoint for partner developers.
output: Purpose: Retrieves one customer record by its stable identifier.
Authentication: Requires a partner access token with customer read permission.
Errors: Explains invalid identifiers, missing records, expired tokens, and rate limits.

output_examples.input: Review our payment API documentation for onboarding gaps.
output: Add a first payment tutorial with prerequisites and expected results.
Provide test credentials, idempotency guidance, and a complete error reference.
Link webhook verification steps from every asynchronous payment flow.

output_examples.input: Outline a migration guide from API version one to version two.
output_examples.output: The guide separates breaking changes, replacement fields, updated authentication, migration steps, validation checks, rollback guidance, and the deprecation timeline.

best_practices: Confirm every documented behavior against the current specification, implementation, or tested response.
Use realistic examples that show authentication, successful responses, common errors, and recovery steps.
Assign ownership and automate validation so documentation changes remain synchronized with API releases.
anti_patterns: Do not invent endpoints, fields, credentials, or response behavior when source details are missing.
Do not publish generated examples without testing them against an approved environment.
Do not hide breaking changes inside general release notes without a dedicated migration path.

faq.question: Which API formats can this skill support?
faq.answer: It covers OpenAPI, AsyncAPI, GraphQL schemas, webhooks, SDK references, and related developer portal content.

faq.question: Can it create an OpenAPI specification from requirements?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide endpoint behavior, schemas, authentication, errors, and examples so the specification reflects the actual API.

faq.question: Does it test generated examples?
faq.answer: No. It can propose testing workflows, but examples must run in an approved environment before publication.

faq.question: Can it design documentation for multiple API versions?
faq.answer: Yes. It can organize versioned references, changelogs, deprecation notices, compatibility details, and migration guidance.

faq.question: Can it generate SDK implementation files?
faq.answer: It can plan SDK generation and document usage. A dedicated generator and language-specific validation are still required.

faq.question: What inputs produce the most accurate documentation?
faq.answer: Provide current specifications, source behavior, audience needs, authentication rules, sample payloads, error cases, release constraints, and documentation platform details.
